security_spec.violation_condition: The Linux kernel executes WRS.NTO in S-mode via __cmpwait() (arch/riscv/include/asm/cmpxchg.h) and smp_cond_load_relaxed() (arch/riscv/include/asm/barrier.h) without configuring or reading mstatus.TW. If firmware (M-mode) sets mstatus.TW=1, a WRS.NTO that exceeds the implementation-specific bounded time limit raises an illegal-instruction exception (scause=2). The kernel's do_trap_insn_illegal() handler in arch/riscv/kernel/traps.c unconditionally panics on illegal instructions in kernel mode, resulting in immediate system halt.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: WRS\.NTO executed in S-mode without mstatus\.TW check or save/restore; illegal-instruction handler unconditionally panics in kernel context
security_spec.summary: Kernel executes WRS.NTO in S-mode via __cmpwait()/smp_cond_load_relaxed() without managing mstatus.TW; firmware-set TW=1 causes unexpected illegal-instruction exception and kernel panic

findings.finding: WRS.NTO is emitted via ZAWRS_WRS_NTO (0x00d00073) in inline asm at lines 393, 410, 421, 432 without any exception-table (_ASM_EXTABLE) entry and without checking mstatus.TW. If firmware (M-mode) sets mstatus.TW=1, a WRS.NTO exceeding the implementation's bounded time limit raises scause=2 (illegal instruction), which fixup_exception() cannot recover because there is no extable entry. The code's own comment at line 364-365 acknowledges this: 'because it has been configured to raise an illegal instruction exception.' Only extension presence (riscv_has_extension_likely()) is checked, not the mstatus.TW trap-enable bit.

smp_cond_load_relaxed() unconditionally calls __cmpwait_relaxed() -> __cmpwait() which emits WRS.NTO. Used in hot spinlock paths: qspinlock slowpath (kernel/locking/qspinlock.c:368), osq_lock (kernel/locking/osq_lock.c:146), and BPF rqspinlock (kernel/bpf/rqspinlock.c:576,608,647). A WRS.NTO trap in any of these paths — especially in interrupt context where die() unconditionally panics — would either halt the system or kill the lock-holder via make_task_dead(), leaving the lock permanently held.
findings.snippet:
#define smp_cond_load_relaxed(ptr, cond_expr) ({                                 \
	typeof(ptr) __PTR = (ptr);                                          \
	__unqual_scalar_typeof(*ptr) VAL;                                   \
	for (;;) {                                                          \
		VAL = READ_ONCE(*__PTR);                                \
		if (cond_expr)                                          \
			break;                                          \
		__cmpwait_relaxed(ptr, VAL);                            \
	}

findings.finding: Kernel-mode exception handling unconditionally calls die() if fixup_exception() returns false. There is no intermediate recovery path for WRS.NTO traps: no attempt to read mstatus.TW, no fallback to a pause-based polling loop, and no handling of the case where the trapping WRS.NTO was in a spinlock-acquisition path. fixup_exception() searches exception tables by epc, and since the WRS.NTO inline asm has no extable entry, it always returns false.

die() has two unconditional panic() paths: (1) in_interrupt() leads to 'panic("Fatal exception in interrupt")' — and WRS.NTO is called from qspinlock/osq_lock paths that may run in IRQ context; (2) panic_on_oops leads to 'panic("Fatal exception")'. Even the non-panic path calls make_task_dead(SIGSEGV), which kills the current task. If that task held a spinlock (the very scenario when WRS.NTO is executing), the lock is never released.

KVM sets HSTATUS_VTW during VCPU reset, which correctly causes guest (VS-mode) WRS.NTO to trap into HS-mode for virtualization. This is correct KVM behavior per the RISC-V hypervisor spec: VTW controls WRS trap-and-emulate for the guest. However, the host kernel (running in HS-mode) itself still has no mstatus.TW protection.

CONFIG_RISCV_ISA_ZAWRS defaults to 'y' with dependency on RISCV_ALTERNATIVE, meaning alternative-patched WRS.NTO sequences will be installed on any Zawrs-capable platform. The config help text mentions WRS.NTO enables 'low-power state' entry but does not document the mstatus.TW interaction or the potentially fatal trap-on-timeout behavior.
findings.snippet:
config RISCV_ISA_ZAWRS
	bool "Zawrs extension support for more efficient busy waiting"
	depends on RISCV_ALTERNATIVE
	default y
	help
	  The Zawrs extension defines instructions to be used in polling loops
	  which allow a hart to enter a low-power state or to trap to the
	  hypervisor while waiting on a store to a memory location.
